questions.question: Define accounting.
questions.solution_html:
• Definition by the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (Year 1961)
  • “Accounting is the art of recording, classifying and summarizing in a significant
  • a financial character, and interpreting the result thereof”.
  • Accounting is the systematic process of recording, classifying, summarising, and
  • interpreting financial transactions to provide useful information for decision-making.
questions.final_answer: interpreting financial transactions to provide useful information for decision-making
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: What is a contra entry? Give two examples
questions.solution_html:
• A contra entry is a transaction recorded on both sides of the cash book, affecting
  • both cash and bank columns simultaneously. Examples: (i) Cash deposited into bank;
  • (ii) Cash withdrawn from bank for office use.
questions.final_answer: (ii) Cash withdrawn from bank for office use

questions.question: Explain that cash book is a journal as well as a ledger account
questions.solution_html:
• As a journal: The cash book records cash and bank transactions chronologically at the
  • time they occur, so it functions as a primary book of original entry (a journal). Each
  • receipt and payment is entered on the date of the transaction (debit for receipts
  • credit for payments) with narration—this fulfils the journal role of recording
  • transactions before ledger posting.
  • As a ledger account: The cash book also acts as the ledger account for cash and bank
  • balances because the balances shown in its cash and bank columns are final, carrying
  • the cumulative effect of transactions. Thus there is no separate cash ledger account
  • required—balances from the cash book are used directly in the Trial Balance and
  • Balance Sheet.
questions.final_answer: Balance Sheet
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: What is imprest system of maintaining Petty cash book
questions.solution_html:
• The imprest system is a method for operating petty cash in which a fixed float
  • (imprest amount) is advanced to a petty cashier to meet small, routine expenditures.
  • At regular intervals the petty cashier presents vouchers for payments made and is
  • reimbursed to restore the float to its original fixed amount. Controls petty
  • expenditure, simplifies accounting for small payments, facilitates verification
  • (vouchers), and reduces administrative burden on the main cash book.
questions.final_answer: (vouchers), and reduces administrative burden on the main cash book
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Question 19
questions.solution_html:
• The Gross Profit Ratio is 25% on sales. If Sales = ₹2,00,000, find Gross Profit and
  • COGS
  • Gross Profit (GP) = 25% of Sales = 0.25 × ₹200,000 = ₹50,000.
  • Cost of Goods Sold = Sales − GP = ₹200,000 − ₹50,000 = ₹150,000.
  • Answer: Gross Profit = ₹50,000; COGS = ₹150,000.
questions.final_answer: Answer: Gross Profit = ₹50,000; COGS = ₹150,000
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Entity and continuity concepts are Inter related?
questions.solution_html:
• Yes. The entity and continuity concepts are inter-related because the entity concept
  • treats the business as a separate, distinct unit from its owners, and the continuity
  • (going concern) concept assumes that this separate entity will continue to operate in
  • the foreseeable future. When both concepts operate together, financial statements
  • are prepared on the basis that the business exists independently from its owners and
  • will continue long enough to utilise assets, settle liabilities, and follow normal
  • accounting processes without the need for liquidation values.
questions.final_answer: accounting processes without the need for liquidation values
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
